title: Audit PR6334 on POSIX with materialized path and alias controls
body:
PR #6334 fixes a local-overlap inventory that normalizes CR/CRLF Git names to LF, but its author explicitly left POSIX execution and symlink coverage open. This independent audit closes that bounded environment gap at `e579ddc0e0b4614184b869f8d20cffdcc26380a6` and supplies a self-contained differential replay.

The new package constructs real CR, LF and CRLF filenames, executable notes and symlinks. Across seven filesystem states, it runs both the pinned canonical-main helper and #6334's helper through their offline JSON CLI. In five incomplete states, main falsely reports complete coverage while #6334 lists the exact two missing paths. Real-note restoration, untracked notes, leaf/parent/dangling aliases, the result limit and unchanged cache bytes are checked. The implementation repair remains credited to josecarlosgonzalezroque-design; no shared helper or selected result is changed here.

### Validation

macOS 26.5 arm64, CPython 3.12.16, Apple Git 2.50.1:

- Predecessor's nine documented modules: **83 tests passed, zero skips**; another **13 optimized-driver executions passed**. All five symlink tests skipped in the original Windows run executed here.
- Independent differential replay: **7 cases × 2 versions**, in normal and optimized modes, all expected results. Every independent CLI child explicitly receives `-O` in optimized mode. The unchanged predecessor local-suite driver's children remain nonoptimized, as documented.
- **5 corrupted source files and 8 forged report fields rejected**, with two positive controls, in both modes.
- Registered four-command package replay, metadata/source pins, committed-byte preflight (28 files), and `git diff --check` pass.
- A committed-source export outside project Git history passes the direct optimized verifier and rejection controls. All five retained source/test files are SHA256-pinned; no cached unmerged commit or network fetch is required.
- Replay planning selects **only this package**, accounting for 4,552 omitted existing manifests.

The unrelated current-main `test_research_current_status.py` has **one reproduced failure out of six tests**: CI documentation still names frontier6030 while selected metadata names frontier7000. Existing #7276 addresses that repair. This submission does not claim globally green tests or perform a scientific cold replay.

### Hosted CI result

[Actions run 43600296628](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/43600296628) completed with failure at the generic onboarding stage: **760 tests, 1 failure, 24 platform skips** (735 passed). The sole failure is exactly the pre-existing `CurrentCiNavigationTests.test_current_ci_section_matches_selected_record` mismatch reproduced above. The package-specific hosted replay was therefore not reached. This does not replace the successful local four-command registered replay and Git-history-free source export.

### Scope, evidence and coordination

[README and exact evidence](https://github.com/FanPUYen/integer-mult-bounds/blob/aa2504ad4aff4af0e558e9f9c66c83fda5f5cb7c/research/pr6334-posix-path-audit/README.md), source origins, original test logs, machine receipts, and explicit replay hooks are included. Base: `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`, priority revision 8. The portable-replay card is retained with an explicit scope change to #6334's handoff. This is evidence for the exact pending head, not the eventual merge result; integration with later main changes remains a separate check.

[Advance claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19612921). Handoff-first and targeted PR/Discussion searches found no matching POSIX audit. The overlap helper refreshed 901 open PR bodies and 7,512 Discussion records. The final PR refresh succeeded; the final Discussion refresh failed with EOF and retained the earlier 13:20 UTC complete snapshot. Sparse local and closed-PR coverage remain limited; no exhaustive novelty claim.

Credit josecarlosgonzalezroque-design (#6334), lee-phys (#4419), Ali Romman (#5725), Nick Petalas (#6161), Douglas Colkitt and retained tool contributors. Prepared by Hao Yan (@FanPUYen) with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance and separately scoped agents for overlap review, test execution, package scaffolding and review. Apache-2.0. No theorem, supplier admission, merge, or selected-frontier change.
